OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN : Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing 
away of Shri P.R. Kumaramangalam, Minister of Power, on the 23rd August, 2000 at 
the young age of 48. 
Born in May, 1952, at Madras, Shri Kumaramangalam had his education at 
Madras University and then got a degree in Law from Delhi University. An active 
student union leader, he was the founder-Presi dent of the N.S.U.I. Subsequently, Shri 
Kumaramangalam was associated with various trade union activities and carved out a 
niche for himself in the trade union movement  in India, with his sharp intellect, 
outstanding negotiating skills and his devotion to the cause. 
"Ranga", as he was popularly know n, had a long and distinguished 
Parliamentary career. He was a Member of the Eighth, Ninth, Tenth, Twelfth and 
Thirteenth Lok Sabhas. He served as a Union Minister for several years and held the 
portfolios of Parliamentary Affairs, Law, Justice and Company Affairs, Science and 
Technology, Electronics, Ocean Developmen t and Power. During his Parliamentary 
career, his grasp of policy, his ability to marshal facts and his formidable debating skills 
were as impressive, as hi s great sense of humour, affability and openness was 
endearing. 
In the untimely passing away of Shri P.R. Kumaramangalam, the country has lost 
an eminent Parliamentarian, an outstanding administrator, a dynamic personality and a 
great crusader for the common man's cause. To me personally, and to all of us, his 
passing away is a great loss and he leaves behind a void, which we will all feel for a 
long time. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect 
to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 1 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2000] 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved family 
our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy. 
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri RR. Kumaramangalam, the House stands 
adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on Friday, the 25th August, 2000. 
The House then adjourned at three past eleven of 
the clock till eleven of the clock on Friday, the 25th August, 2000.
